key_insight: PIWF splits multiscale flow learning into Fourier modes for global coherence and wavelets for localized sharp features, then enforces physics through the loss.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical surrogate for fluid problems with shocks, fronts, wakes, and vortices when dense interior measurements are unavailable.
method: Fourier branch models long-range coherent structures.
Wavelet branch captures compact, steep-gradient and vortical features.
Residual MLP with channel attention fuses both branches under physics-informed constraints.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on five canonical flow problems—Burgers, shallow water, Kovasznay flow, Taylor–Green vortex, and 2D cylinder wake—and reported better capture of gradients, interfaces, wakes, vortices, and spectra than PINNs and PI-KANs.
watch_item: Performance may depend on careful balancing of Fourier and wavelet branches plus the physics-loss terms, which can be sensitive for complex geometries or noisy boundary data.
paper_title: Physics informed wavelet Fourier representation for multiscale fluid dynamics
